title: How remote assistance rates are measured for robotaxis

title: Fear that big platforms could embrace and extinguish Mastodon

why: Venting about an unversioned legacy codebase, a lone developer, and a hiring setback; asks for resources without offering technical insight.

title: Argument for imperial units' divisibility

why: Cultural critique of instant-replay style sharing; essayistic opinion built on anecdotes rather than verifiable insight.

title: Satirical take on crowdfunding pledges for Mozilla

title: Technology, incentives, and pointless employment

title: Working with ADHD on pair programming and TDD
why: Personal account of how ADHD shapes coding style and communication; valuable perspective but largely self-description without a transferable technique.

title: Why open plans can help team productivity
why: Cornell study: open layouts make it easier to read availability, manage quick interruptions, and ask low-stakes questions, boosting team creativity and output.

title: Why tourists crowd famous parks but skip nearby sites
why: Traveler observation about crowding at famous parks; opinion-driven, with the gate-and-ranger point a loose explanation.

title: Ember documentation dispute and forum norms
why: Community moderation spat over tone and documentation feedback; interpersonal context, not transferable technical knowledge.

title: Why Homebrew mirrors older macOS package managers

title: Anticompetitive conduct versus monopoly status
why: Argues Apple's app store issue is anticompetitive behavior rather than monopoly; a persuasive framing but primarily a policy argument.

title: Political commentary on election data narratives
why: Partisan argument about voters and Facebook data controversies; opinion-driven, not a technical or factual lesson.

title: Career advice for unlucky circumstances
why: Lists forms of bad luck such as timing, lacking networks, and credentials; a thoughtful framing, but not a concrete practical guide.

title: Test scores track GPA closely in admissions
why: Former admissions reader: SAT/ACT scores correlated strongly with GPA, often predicting admit or deny decisions before normalizing transcripts.

title: Chrome exploit shows limits of C++ security

title: Why sanitation needs behavior change, not just toilets
why: Argues people already know not to drink where they defecate; skeptical take on infrastructure versus behavior, supported by anecdote only.

title: Google's alleged isolation of Windows Phone
why: One-sided narrative of Google blocking Windows Phone apps, with an alleged YouTube example; unverified claims rather than a settled history.

title: Personal experience contradicting psilocybin hype
why: Counter-anecdote that depression relief from trips fades within months; personal experience, not controlled evidence.

title: Why HN keeps an overheated discussion detector
why: Moderator explanation of an automated penalty system; procedural and community-specific rather than generally instructive knowledge.

title: Interruptions affect all deep work, not just programming

title: Founder describes domain suspension with no notice

title: Disagreement with Stallman's views on privacy

title: Musical notation mismatch with twelve-tone chords
why: Asks whether notation could improve on staff lines given twelve-tone equal temperament; a question shaped by personal dyslexia, not a settled explanation.

why: Complaint that Atlassian left on-premise customers without a migration path; sentiment about vendor support rather than general knowledge.

why: Bulge bracket analysts get roughly $70k base plus bonus; most leave after two years, few reach associate, and associates often come via MBA.

title: Critique of a talk on programming paradigms
why: Argues the talk romanticizes untried ideas and dismisses text-based programming without evidence; critique of rhetoric, not a technical lesson.

title: South Africa's vaccine rollout crisis and politics
why: Detailed local political context about a vaccine suspension, but mainly grievances and national politics rather than transferable knowledge.

title: Why early equity rounds can hurt founders
why: Equity rounds force a valuation when founders are weakest and add strings; founder loans, convertible notes, or services revenue may be better early options.

title: What actually makes a market a bubble
why: A bubble is rapid valuation growth followed by collapse big enough to hinder investment and innovation; compares 2008 housing and dotcom, noting startup costs differ.

title: Moderator essay on responsibility in conversation
why: Community-norms essay about commenters' responsibility to their audience; an ethical argument from a moderator, not a technical explanation.

title: How to negotiate buying a domain you want
why: Don't ask for a favor; owners know their domain's value. Let them name a price, since a domain is worth only what buyers pay.

title: Rebuttal to claims arts are underappreciated

title: Account of DigitalOcean sponsorship cancellation

title: Student rebuts professor about cheating and ratings
why: Personal dispute over teaching ratings and classroom treatment; interpersonal, not a transferable insight.

title: Documenting Syria protests through live streams
why: Firsthand account of citizen media during the uprising; powerful testimony but mainly historical narrative without technical explanation.

title: Why console unit sales mislead about profitability
why: Consoles often sell at a loss; profits come from games and services, so installed base and software attach rate matter more than hardware unit counts.

title: Apple's integration advantage in headphones
why: Argues Apple wins where hardware-software integration and low tolerance for issues matter; a consumer preference opinion.

title: 25% tariff hits makers buying electronic components
why: Hobbyist reports cost impact and posts a tariff code list; news reaction without explaining how the schedule works.

title: Why patent examiners reject impossible inventions
why: Patents must enable a skilled person to build the invention without undue experimentation; examiners reject perpetual-motion-style claims, though this one still issued.

title: Restricted stock taxes and the 83(b) election
why: Without a timely 83(b) election, restricted stock is taxed as ordinary income at each vesting; electing at grant makes later gains capital gains.

title: Tactics for disrupting fascist events
why: Activist describes denying venues and political critiques; a movement-politics account rather than neutral technical or factual knowledge.

title: Free TPU research compute for ML hackers

why: GrapheneOS's network toggle blocks direct and indirect access, while CalyxOS lets apps bypass its firewall through INTERNET-gated APIs; concrete privacy architecture comparison.

title: Estimating US interceptor stockpile depletion

title: Why Silicon Valley's money focus attracts talent

title: Personal account of isolation and declining health
why: Anecdote about remote work loneliness and health decline; relatable but personal, not substantiated by the study it cites.

title: Modular monoliths as a middle ground to microservices

title: Political views flip like a spinning illusion

title: Anecdote about Google's lack of account support

why: Opinion on managers, anti-intellectualism, and where tech careers go; essayistic with little concrete information.

why: Argues remote preferences depend on home and office quality; reasonable framing, but opinion-level commentary rather than evidence.

title: Personal shift away from online communication

why: Puzzled musing about why violent games are accepted while other taboos are not; reflective opinion without evidence.
